name: Ronghe QIU
institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
bio: I am a Ph.D. candidate in Artificial Intelligence at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou), advised by Junwei Liang and co-supervised by Ying-Cong Chen. I obtained my M.Phil. degree in Artificial Intelligence from the same university in 2024 under the supervision of Junwei Liang. My research focuses on embodied AI for long-horizon mobile manipulation. I am particularly interested in how robots can reason through complex tasks and generalize to new tasks and environments.

projects.title: Agentic Robot Tour Guide
details: Developed automated mapping and relocalization using point cloud features for navigation in dynamic indoor environments.
Designed a skill-based agent framework in which a VLM calls navigation, speech, and gesture actions in response to user commands.
Enabled multimodal interaction through real-time text-to-speech and internet-connected knowledge retrieval.

projects.title: Multi-Floor Robot Navigation
details: Deployed the VLFM algorithm on Unitree Go2, bridging the simulation-to-reality gap for mapping and path planning.
Integrated navigation and elevator manipulation into a unified pipeline.

experience.title: Project Manager
details: Led a team providing U.S. capital market IPO services, including reporting, internal control examination, and operating results analysis.
Provided financial due diligence for acquisitions and investments, and offered investment advice.
Managed client relationships and expanded the client base.

experience.title: Senior Auditor
details: Provided audit services for clients listed in different capital markets under tight schedules.
Identified significant audit risks and designed procedures to address them.

meditation: Since high school, I have been drawn to Zen, Indian yoga, and the exploration of superconscious states. The ideas of Jiddu Krishnamurti and Swami Vivekananda have had a lasting influence on me.
For me, studying AI and practicing meditation are both ways of better understanding what it means to be human.
background: I received my bachelor's degree in Finance from Sun Yat-sen University and worked in finance for four years, primarily advising companies on IPOs in the U.S. market.
motivation: Inspired by the belief that technology can change the world for the better, I transitioned to AI research. I hope to help build a future where more people can live in peace and happiness.
